podcast.title: Local Sensation
podcast.body: Born in the Flood was Nathaniel Rateliff's first band and achieved a "local sensation" status, with The New York Times calling Rateliff a "folk pop hero." "His first band was called Born in the Flood. They were, you know, something of a local sensation. The New York Times even called him a folk pop hero."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Career Challenges
xref.body: After his initial band Born in the Flood, and subsequent solo work, Nathaniel Rateliff released multiple records and played hundreds of gigs, receiving good reviews but struggling to achieve significant financial success, making a "hard living." "Reviews were generally good, but that really didn't translate into any big paydays. Yes, it was a living, but it was a hard one."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rejected Record Deal
xref.body: During his time with Born in the Flood, Nathaniel Rateliff turned down an indie record deal, despite his band being a "local sensation" and receiving praise from The New York Times. "There was an indie album, but for some reason Nathaniel turned down a record deal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Relocation to Denver (Age 18)
xref.body: Nathaniel Rateliff moved from Missouri to Denver at the age of 18, where he would later form his first band, Born in the Flood. "He relocated from Missouri to Denver when he was 18."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
